html:
Prithvi Narayan Shah was the king of the small hill state of Gorkha who conquered the Kathmandu valley in 1768 and founded the kingdom of Nepal.

He became king of Gorkha in 1743, at twenty. It was one of about fifty little states in the central Himalayas. To the east lay the rich Kathmandu valley, held by three rival Newar kingdoms that lived on the trade between India and Tibet.

He took twenty-five years over it. He bought muskets in Varanasi, seized the hill of Nuwakot on the Tibet road in 1744, and then closed the valley's trade routes one after another. The town of Kirtipur beat him off twice before it fell. An East India Company force sent to help the valley in 1767 was defeated in the foothills. Kathmandu fell in September 1768 while its people were celebrating a festival, and the other two cities the next year.

He moved his capital to Kathmandu and pushed on east. He expelled the Catholic missionaries and kept out foreign traders. His advice to his heirs called Nepal a yam between two boulders, China and British India, to be kept safe by friendship with both and trust in neither.

His heirs carried the conquests further until the Anglo-Nepalese War. His family reigned until 2008.
